assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, actions on islets, appetite and gastric emptying) led to durable-acting agonists that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with outcome benefits in cardiovascular and renal disease. Originality, clarity and very large clinical and societal impact make it a leading candidate.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its secretion), Drucker (mechanisms of action and therapeutic concept) and Knudsen (design of the long-acting agonist liraglutide/semaglutide) span basic to translational contributions. Mojsov's peptide-identification role and the contributions of Habener and others (not in the credited list) make allocation contentious; I choose three from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many large randomized outcome trials over more than a decade; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair apportionment among Mojsov, Habener and the credited names is disputed and I have not verified the details.
A compound story (basic physiology versus drug engineering) may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signaling, with IRE1/HAC1 splicing and downstream pathways. It is a clean, conceptual discovery that is now central to understanding proteostasis, secretory-cell physiology and disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are widely credited with the decisive discovery and mechanism (Kozutsumi/Ron/Sidrauski and others contributed); a two-laureate prize is a coherent configuration from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation across yeast and mammals; mature and stable, timely for recognition.
uncertainties: Contributions of trainees and collaborators outside the credited list are not assessed.
Direct therapeutic impact is still emerging, though this is not required for a fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed against tumour antigens created a new class of living therapeutics, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and multiple approved products. Originality, clinical efficacy and breadth of follow-on work are substantial.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design and costimulation), June (clinical translation and CD19 CAR-T) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells) give a plausible trio; Eshhar and others who preceded them are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Several years of clinical follow-up and multiple independent approvals; maturity is good for hematologic cancers, less so for solid tumours.
uncertainties: Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work is outside the credited names and complicates priority.
Limitations in solid tumours and long-term toxicity are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with light and became a core tool across neuroscience; channelrhodopsin discovery plus its deployment in neurons were both transformative.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth, Boyden and others demonstrated neuronal use; Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck are also credited, so any trio leaves out a plausible laureate and credit allocation is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and in routine use for about 15 years; mature for a tool, with clinical applications (e.g. vision restoration) only beginning.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited names is unresolved.
Whether the Committee prefers a tool or a therapeutic/physiological discovery is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic definition of SMN2 splicing correction and its development into nusinersen produced a disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a clear example of RNA-targeted medicine moving from mechanism to cure-like benefit.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are a natural pair; other contributors to the development program are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical data; the interpretation is stable and recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: The relative weight of academic mechanism versus industrial development is unresolved.
Long-term durability data continue to accumulate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR defined a central nutrient- and growth-factor-sensing pathway controlling cell growth, with relevance to cancer, metabolism, immunology and ageing. The discovery is fundamental and broadly important.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and established its role in growth control; Sabatini identified mTOR and its regulators, but Schreiber's drug-target work complicates allocation. I select the two names with the clearest conceptual contributions.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with decades of confirmation; rapalogs are clinically used, though clinical benefit is moderate.
uncertainties: Relative roles of Schreiber and Sabatini in credit allocation are uncertain and not verified here.
Other contributors (Heitman, Rall, Brown, Sabers) are not in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified a neuropeptide system governing wakefulness, with loss of orexin neurons explaining narcolepsy type 1, and has led to orexin receptor antagonists and agonists. It is a clear physiological and disease-mechanism discovery.
assessment.attribution: Yanagisawa and Sakurai discovered orexin and its receptors; Mignot's canine genetics and human narcolepsy link provide the disease connection; de Lecea and Kilduff made independent hypocretin discoveries, so a three-person limit forces difficult omissions.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed for over 25 years with approved dual orexin antagonists; stable, though orexin agonist therapies are still maturing.
uncertainties: Parallel independent discoveries by two groups complicate priority.
Allocation among five names is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL11A as the repressor of fetal hemoglobin explains hemoglobin switching and enabled therapeutic reactivation; the first gene-editing-based therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia rests on this work. It combines human genetics, mechanism and treatment.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran led the key mechanistic and genetic work; Bauer contributed to the enhancer-editing therapeutic strategy; Thein's GWAS contribution is also credited. Several plausible trios exist.
assessment.maturity: Therapy approved only recently, so long-term clinical outcomes are limited; the basic mechanism is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Premature relative to some other candidates because of limited long-term follow-up.
Credit with Thein and earlier fetal hemoglobin researchers is not fully resolved.
